types.explanation: RFC 5321 defines 220 as a positive completion reply indicating the SMTP service is ready; RFC 3207 also uses 220 to accept STARTTLS.
RFC 5321 defines 221 as a positive completion reply indicating the SMTP service is closing the transmission channel.
RFC 5321 defines 250 as a positive completion reply indicating the requested mail action was completed; RFC 2920, RFC 3030, and RFC 3207 use it for successful EHLO, BDAT, and capability responses.
RFC 5321 specifies 252 when the server cannot verify the user but will accept the message and attempt delivery.
RFC 5321 defines 354 as a positive intermediate reply instructing the client to start mail input; RFC 2920 shows it as the DATA prompt.
RFC 5321 defines 503 as a permanent negative completion reply for a bad command sequence; RFC 4954 requires 503 for AUTH issued during a mail transaction or after successful authentication.
RFC 3207 specifies 530 to require STARTTLS before other commands, and 5.7.0 as the enhanced status code when ENHANCEDSTATUSCODES is in use.
RFC 5321 defines 550 as a permanent negative completion reply indicating the requested action was not taken because the mailbox is unavailable; RFC 2920 shows 550 for disallowed RCPT commands.
RFC 5321 defines 554 as a permanent negative completion reply indicating the transaction failed; RFC 2920 shows 554 when no valid recipients are supplied.
